predecessors.note: Infobox 'Preceded by: Wari Empire and Killke culture'; the page describes no handover and the Wari state ended long before 1200 (dossier wari-empire).

successors.note: The Inca Empire dossier starts in 1438 on the same ground.

rulers.name: Manco Capac
rulers.note: Infobox reign dates, all 'c.'; a traditional chronology, the first rulers legendary. The text dates Yawar Waqaq c. 1380-c. 1400 and Viracocha Inca c. 1400-c. 1438, ten years earlier than the infobox.

rulers.name: Viracocha Inca
rulers.note: Infobox c. 1410-1438; drawn to 1437 (the Inca Empire starts 1438).

correction.text: Cliopatria's 1294 Cusco shape applied from c. 1200: the Cusco valley and the Huatanay river, 'a small city-state'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the infobox gives 'Manco Capac organized the Kingdom of Cusco: c. 1200' and the lead 'a small city-state founded by the Incas around the start of 13th century'; Cliopatria's first Cuzco shape begins in 1294. The page gives no area; the 1294 shape is applied from 1200 although a 'small city-state' may have been smaller.

8,783 km2 round Cusco for 1294-1401. The page centres the kingdom on 'the Cusco valley and the Huatanay river' and gives no area or border; no dated change in these years (Ayarmaca and Quechua conflicts are undated beyond reigns), so the shape stands unverified in extent.

Same 8,783 km2 shape for 1402-1430. Under Viracocha Inca (c. 1410-1438) the page has an invasion of the Yucay and Calca valleys without a year; the shape does not include Calca, so the gain is a ledger event (confidence 1) rather than a shape change.

correction.text: unchanged shape, years 1431-1437; from 1438 the same ground is the Inca Empire's

keyframe_review.note: Same shape; valid only to 1437. The Chanka-Inca War is c. 1438 on Rowe's chronology (del Busto 1424-25, Dammert 1430-1440) and the infobox gives 'Establishment of the Inca Empire'; the Kingdom of Cusco page gives 'The Inca Empire 1438-1533'. The Inca Empire dossier starts in 1438, so the Cuzco shape runs 1431-1437.

region.text: the Cusco valley and the Huatanay river

ledger.note: c. 1200: Manco Capac founds the Kingdom of Cusco. Infobox 'Manco Capac organized the Kingdom of Cusco: c. 1200'; 'began as a small city-state founded by the Incas around the start of 13th century'. The migration legend from Lake Titicaca and Pacaritambo is undated.

c. 1350: the Hanan Cusco line takes the throne. 'Inca Roca became the first Hanan Cusco ruler' around c. 1350 after overthrowing Capac Yupanqui with Hanan Cusco support; the page calls the Hurin dynasty a rival line and dates no division. Same state, colour continues.

region.text: the Yucay and Calca valleys of the Urubamba (the Sacred Valley of the Incas)

ledger.counterpart: Yucay and Calca valley groups (unnamed on the page)
ledger.note: Viracocha Inca invades the Yucay and Calca valleys. The page gives no year (his reign is c. 1410-1438 in the infobox, c. 1400-1438 in the text) and lists the valleys among places where groups expelled from Cusco had gone ('Sacred Valley of the Incas'); placed at the start of his reign, page silent on the date.

c. 1438: the Chanka war transforms the kingdom. The war's date is uncertain ('The exact date of the conflict is unknown'; Rowe 1438, del Busto 1424-25, Dammert 1430-1440); the infobox gives 'Inca victory; Establishment of the Inca Empire' and the Chanka confederation is annexed. The Cusco shape passes to the Inca Empire; drawn as 1437 so the Inca Empire starts in the infobox year 1438.

c. 1438: the Kingdom of Cusco becomes the Inca Empire. 'The Inca Empire 1438-1533' (lead); Viracocha Inca ruled to c. 1438 and Cusi Yupanqui (Pachacuti) defeated the Chanka c. 1438 (infobox). The land goes whole to the Inca Empire.

wars.name: Ayarmaca conflict under Lloque Yupanqui
wars.outcome: Lloque Yupanqui (c. 1260-1290) fights the Ayarmaca, exploiting the death of their leader Tocay Capac in combat; the page gives no territorial result.
wars.note: No zone: the page names no land and no year inside the reign.

wars.name: Chanka-Inca War

zones.text: the Chanka confederation's land: the infobox lists the location as Cusco, Andahuaylas and Apurímac

wars.outcome: Inca victory under Cusi Yupanqui (Pachacuti); the Chanka army 'entire army annihilated' (infobox); establishment of the Inca Empire and annexation of the Chanka confederation. Battle at Ichupampa.
wars.note: Date uncertain: Rowe 1438; del Busto 1424-25; Dammert between 1430 and 1440. Inca Roca (c. 1350-1380) had already 'driven them back to Andahuaylas' (Kingdom of Cusco page). The war itself is drawn from the Inca Empire dossier (gain 1438).

certainty.note: No border is described by any page; the shape is Cliopatria's approximation of the Cusco valley.

sources.title: Kingdom of Cusco
sources.note: Identity, c. 1200 foundation, rulers with c. dates (infobox), Hanan dynasty c. 1350, Ayarmaca, Chanka, Yucay and Calca, succession by the Inca Empire; no area given.

sources.title: Chanka-Inca War
sources.note: Date of the war (Rowe 1438; del Busto 1424-25; Dammert 1430-1440), combatants, Inca victory, annexation of the Chanka confederation.

notes:
Cliopatria's 'Cuzco' (1294-1439) is three identical 8,783 km2 shapes at Cusco; the Wikipedia field of the row is the city 'Cusco' and the state article is 'Kingdom of Cusco', which is the page used. Start moved to c. 1200 (infobox) from 1294; end set to 1437 so the Inca Empire (infobox 1438) does not overlap: the transition year is itself uncertain (Chanka-Inca War: Rowe 1438, del Busto 1424-25, Dammert 1430-1440).
The page gives no area and no border; every verdict on the shape is 'extent unverified'. The ruler dates are the infobox's 'c.' dates of a traditional list (text and infobox differ by ten years for Yawar Waqaq and Viracocha Inca); the early kings are legendary.
Counterparts without dossiers: Chanka confederation (Andahuaylas/Apurimac; Chanka are named as a belligerent only, group am-04 could add them but the pages give no reign or boundary), Ayarmaca, the Yucay/Calca valley groups (unnamed). 'Sacred Valley of the Incas' is not a gazetteer region name (a coordinate disc stands in for it).
Page budget: 2 pages (Kingdom of Cusco; Chanka-Inca War).
